groundTruth.rootCauseReason: A schema change added a synchronous outbound call per record, which tripled per-message processing time; the consumers stayed alive and kept polling, so the lag was produced by consumer-side throughput rather than by broker capacity.

rootCauseIndicators.description: 4.2 million messages of lag accumulated over six hours
the consumers are alive and polling, which separates a stuck consumer group from a slow one

causalChain.mechanism: per-message processing time tripled, so the group drained the topic more slowly than it was written and the lag grew monotonically for six hours

evidenceCheckpoints.description: lag accumulated across the six-hour window, in messages, and it accumulated on the group rather than on the topic: the broker served what it had while the consumers drained it more slowly, which is the reading that separates this case from a broker at capacity
per-message processing time after the schema change, as the ratio of the post reading to the baseline one

remediation.action: move the outbound call off the consume path, or batch it, and let the group drain

query: Consumer group order-events accumulated 4.2 million messages of lag over six hours while the consumers stayed alive and polling; per-message processing time tripled after a schema change. What failed?
